sections.h2: Why Businesses Trust Teknoppy's Website Cost Calculator

items.text: This Website Cost Calculator Kerala tool is calibrated against the actual price bands Teknoppy quotes on live projects across our Website Design, WordPress, Ecommerce, and Web Application services, not arbitrary numbers picked to look competitive.
The range you see is the range you get quoted; we do not publish low numbers to get you on a call and raise them later.
Every add-on shows its own cost impact instead of folding it into one opaque total.

sections.h2: What A Real Estimate Looks Like

paragraphs.text: A small business owner in Kochi recently used the Website Cost Calculator Kerala tool for a six-page business site with SEO setup and content writing included.

The estimate came back with a clear range and a line-item breakdown, base cost, per-page cost, and add-on costs shown separately, with a note that the price would only shift if extra features were added later, never silently.

items.text: No, it is a range based on your selections; a final quote confirms the exact number.

items.title: What if my project does not fit the standard options?
items.text: Complex projects are flagged and routed to a direct quote instead of a guess.

items.q: How accurate is the Website Cost Calculator Kerala estimate?
items.a: It reflects the same pricing bands Teknoppy quotes on real projects, accurate for standard scopes.

items.q: Does the Website Cost Calculator Kerala tool include hosting and domain costs?
items.a: No, it estimates development cost only; hosting and maintenance are shown separately in a full quote.

items.q: Can I use this for an ecommerce website?
items.a: Yes, selecting Ecommerce adjusts the calculator for product catalog size and payment gateway integration.

items.q: Is the Website Cost Calculator Kerala tool really free?
items.a: Yes, with no charge and no obligation to proceed afterward.

devNotes.source: Leadgen pillar page-website cost calculator inner page.pdf (Google Drive, teknoppybusiness@gmail.com)
devNotes.keyword: Website Cost Calculator Kerala — 13 occurrences, density band 1.8–2.0% per the source doc.
devNotes.notRendered: The doc's header block (word count, density, schema list) and its closing cannibalization check are build instructions, not page copy.
devNotes.pricingProvenance: Every band in calculator.types[] is copied from a pricing table already published on a pillar page — web-design.json (business tiers), wordpress.json, ecommerce.json and web-application.json. The page copy promises 'the range you see is the range you get quoted', so nothing here may be computed from an unpublished rate. When a pillar's table changes, change it here too.
devNotes.addonPricing: NEEDS CLIENT: no add-on rate is published anywhere on the site, so SEO setup, content writing and payment gateway integration render as 'Priced in your written quote' rather than an invented figure. Fill in min/max on calculator.addons[] and the calculator will add them to the range and show them as their own line in the breakdown — which is what the doc's 'base cost, per-page cost, and add-on costs shown separately' asks for.
devNotes.perPageCost: The published bands are per page-range (5–8, 10–20, 20–40), not per page, so page count is a band selector rather than a multiplier. A true per-page line item needs a published per-page rate.
devNotes.emailEstimate: 'Email myself this estimate' is a prefilled mailto: link carrying the breakdown, so no address is collected before a number is shown — the doc promises 'No email required to see your estimate.'
devNotes.schemaNote: The doc specifies Product schema. Emitted with an AggregateOffer whose lowPrice/highPrice are the lowest and highest published bands (Rs. 15,000 landing page → Rs. 40,00,000 enterprise application), so Product's required offer field carries real figures rather than an invented one.
